name: SAKE
description: sake-lalm/SAKE dataset hosted on Hugging Face and contributed by the HF Datasets community
rai:dataLimitations: This dataset (SAKE) covers 24 auditory perceptual concepts spanning speech and non-speech domains, but excludes subjective properties such as pitch or loudness, as these lack broad social consensus for defining objective editing targets. The dataset adopts an application-agnostic formulation and evaluates primarily based on post-edit behavior, without requiring the base model's pre-edit prediction to be correct.
rai:dataBiases: The audio sources in this dataset inherit the characteristic distributions of their underlying corpora. Speech and audio data are sourced from Common Voice, CREMA-D, ESC-50, and the Animal-Sound Dataset. Linguistically, the dataset only covers specific languages (English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean), which may lead to biased generalization capabilities of models toward uncovered languages, cultural backgrounds, or regional accents.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: This dataset contains the following sensitive categories: Gender and Language. It includes real speech samples labeled with auditory perceptual concepts that directly cover speaker characteristics (Male, Female) and linguistic features (English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean).
rai:dataUseCases: This dataset is designed to evaluate the performance of knowledge editing methods applied to auditory perceptual knowledge within large audio-language models (LALMs). Validated use cases include comprehensively evaluating the reliability, generality, locality, and portability of knowledge editing methods under single and sequential editing scenarios. This benchmark is explicitly not validated or recommended for direct fine-tuning of production systems, nor should a single metric (e.g., high reliability) be used as proof that an editing method achieves deep knowledge updating and successfully maintains multi-hop reasoning capabilities.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive impact: Provides the first comprehensive evaluation benchmark for editing auditory perceptual knowledge including fine-grained locality decomposition, and establishes that tuning the modality connector serves as a more principled foundation for future knowledge editing, helping to reduce concept entanglement and increase portability. Risks: Misuse of the dataset or editing methodologies to maliciously alter a model's auditory perception or inject biased associations; careless application of edits that induces severe intra-category knowledge entanglement, disrupts multi-hop reasoning (portability failures), or triggers semantic degeneration. Mitigation: The dataset is explicitly designated for research and evaluation purposes. Furthermore, the benchmark comprehensively documents the risks of entanglement and portability failures, explicitly advocating for modality connector tuning as a more balanced and less entanglement-prone direction for auditory-specific editing.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Audio and Knowledge Source Collection
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Audio samples and their corresponding concept labels were directly extracted from established speech and audio corpora, including Common Voice, CREMA-D, ESC-50, and the Animal-Sound Dataset. For the portability evaluation, related world knowledge attributes (e.g., animal diet, locomotion, physical traits) were systematically collected by human. Out-of-scope tasks for general auditory capability were sourced from Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2, and textual QA pairs were sourced from MMLU.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: LLM-Assisted Question Generation and Target Construction
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: Textual concept recognition questions and their semantically equivalent paraphrased variations were generated using GPT-5 (gpt-5-2025-08-07). Reference answers for portability questions were constructed to ensure they are uniquely valid for the edited target concept and not applicable to the original concept.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Ambiguity Filtering
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: During the construction of portability queries, questions whose reference answers were valid for both the original concept and the target concept were manually filtered out to prevent ambiguous evaluation results. Tasks from Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2 were manually reviewed and filtered to exclude any tasks overlapping with the 24 specific concepts evaluated in the benchmark.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.prov:label: Human Verification
prov:wasGeneratedBy.sc:description: All generated text and question-answer pairs underwent a strict four-stage verification process by a team of three human annotators. This included verifying audio-label alignment, checking text question correctness and semantic equivalence, fact-checking portability answers against reference knowledge bases (e.g., Wikipedia), and ensuring cross-annotator agreement. Only instances approved by all three annotators were included in the final dataset.
